title: Normal play
instructions: Move with W A S D, aim with the mouse, shoot the bot in the lane. Nothing is wrong here.

card.what_this_tests: Ordinary movement and shooting make no case.
card.player_can_know: Yes: the bot is in the open lane, in plain sight.
card.server_knows: Vision known on every aimed shot; every speed sample under the cap; every accepted shot on the rifle's cycle.
card.expected_fpsdet_behavior: insufficient_data: not a clean verdict. One player is not a human baseline, so the aim numbers are never compared; the gear rules and the information checks still run and find nothing. fpsdet writes clean only when at least one number was actually compared against a thick enough cohort.
card.invalid_if: Any review or watch appears, or the knowledge chip reads anything but known while the bot is in view.

caveats: With no frozen baseline the aim numbers (accuracy, headshots, distance) are never compared: a server with one player has no humans to compare against, and fpsdet says insufficient_data rather than clean.
actor: NO STAND-IN: the person at the keyboard, or in qualification the honest autopilot (scripted, not a human)
